text: Are we starting to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
You show that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

versions.text: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
versions.explanation: The participle φανερούμενοι is nominative plural, agreeing with "you" (the Corinthians), i.e. "you are being shown/revealed to be." The impersonal "It is clear that" loses the sense that the readers themselves are the visible evidence, and it also weakens the connection to the preceding verse.

text: Such is the confidence we have toward God through Christ.
Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim anything as coming from us; our competence comes from God,
who has made us competent as ministers of a new covenant—not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

Now if the ministry that brought death, engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, a glory that was fading away,
how much greater will be the glory of the ministry of the Spirit?
For if the ministry that brought condemnation had glory, how much more does the ministry that brings righteousness overflow with glory!
Indeed, what once had glory has no glory now in comparison with the glory that surpasses it.
For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of what endures!
Since we have such a hope, we act with great boldness.
We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
But their minds were hardened. To this day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read; it has not been lifted, because it is in Christ that it is set aside.

versions.text: But their minds were hardened. To this day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read; it has not been lifted, because only in Christ is it set aside.
versions.explanation: The word "only" is not in the Greek. The emphasis carried by the word order (ἐν Χριστῷ first) can be reproduced with a cleft construction ("it is in Christ that...") without adding an exclusive term not present in the text.

text: Yes, to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts.
But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with unveiled faces, beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into that same image, from glory to glory—which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

versions.text: And all of us, with unveiled faces, beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into his very image, from glory to glory—which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
versions.explanation: τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα is "the same image" (i.e., the image we behold). "His very image" supplies a pronoun not in the Greek and narrows the sense; "that same image" keeps the link with the mirrored glory just mentioned while reading just as smoothly aloud.
